top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) rest on a genuine physical insight, the magic-wavelength cancellation of the trap light shift, which lets many neutral atoms be interrogated together while keeping ion-level control of systematic shifts. It is independently reproduced in laboratories on several continents that compare clocks at the 1e-18 level, and the two-name allocation is clean. The citation can be kept to the lattice clock and distinguished from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a mature and well-confirmed topological insulator prize that I rank second, with some attribution cost (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Hasan, Fu and Moore left out), and I defer to colleagues on condensed matter. Either is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Katori and Ye are in my own field of atomic and precision physics but I have no documented collaboration with either. My long-time collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) does not bear on this slate.
